title: CPUNET duplicate-singleton sweep (P4 iteration 28)
why: Ten consecutive net blockers had one root pattern: a recovered copy of an SDK unit keeping SEPARATE STATE from a stock unit the same link also contains.  Each was found only when it crashed.  This sweep looks for the whole class mechanically instead.

detector_1_byte_identity: Index every .text.* input section of every stock archive member this net link consumes -- all 40 build archives except our own app/libapp.a, plus the toolchain libgcc and picolibc multilibs -- with a 4-byte mask at every relocation offset.  2506 sections indexed.

For each of the 980 RETAINED recovered net functions, read the shipped netcore_image.bin at its analysis VA for each candidate section length and require agreement on EVERY unmasked byte of the WHOLE section.
This is the evidence bar the task demands -- relocation-masked BYTE identity, never instruction shape (iteration 20's bt_ancs_register_attr mistake).
detector_2_shipped_state_attribution: For every located section, resolve every R_ARM_ABS32 relocation into a .bss.* / .data.* object of the same member:  shipped_address = image_word(hit_va + reloc_off) - in_place_addend.
That yields a map  shipped RAM address -> stock-owned mutable object: iteration 27's stock-.data-window proof generalised to .bss and to every unit, WITHOUT needing a shipped link map.

Cross-reference every attributed address against every retained recovered source (pin name from recon/symbols/g1_net_globals.ld, G1N_ macro, raw literal) to answer 'does something I am KEEPING still own a copy?'.
detector_3_unit_completeness: Slide every section of a candidate unit over the WHOLE shipped image.  A unit may only be displaced WHOLE: if some of its functions are byte-exact and others are not, displacing the exact ones would SPLIT the file-static state between two translation units -- the very defect being removed.
tools: scratchpad i28/sweep_singletons.py, attribute_state.py, hazard_xref.py, scan_unit.py, rank.py, cmpsec.py, gaps.py (analysis-only, outside the repo; no tools/ logic was changed)

caveat_on_sections_not_located: 'sections_not_located' counts stock sections the sliding scan did not find in the shipped image.  A section can be missing for TWO reasons: the shipped link garbage-collected it, or Even's build produced different code.  Where the located sections tile a contiguous VA run with no gaps AND no retained reconstruction inside that run failed to match, the unit is COMPLETE.  esb.c is the unit where the distinction is proven the hard way: eight RETAINED reconstructions lie inside esb.c's own VA run 0x01032764..0x01033b18 (0x1032a3c, 0x1032be4, 0x1032c28, 0x1032de4, 0x1032e54, 0x10331c8, 0x10333b4, 0x1033660) and match NO esb.c section, so esb.c is genuinely vendored/reconfigured by Even and its reconstruction is KEPT.
liveness_note: MEASURED on /private/tmp/g1-i28c-net: of every remaining ranked candidate, only sem.c's z_impl_k_sem_take (FUN_0103689c) and its sibling FUN_01036824 (z_impl_k_sem_give) survive --gc-sections in the link at all.  Every other hazard the sweep found is LATENT -- the reconstruction is already dropped.  That is why the remaining ranked rows are not displaced: they would change nothing measurable and each carries regression risk (iteration 26's 39-row zephyr_drivers batch).
